version.changelog:
clawd-zero-trust v1.2.0 adds dynamic provider whitelisting and improves configuration management.

- Added dynamic whitelisting via scripts/whitelist.sh for secure, user-friendly provider/domain additions.
- Introduced config/custom-providers.json and config/providers.txt for external provider/domain configuration.
- Updated egress-filter.sh to consume new config files, reducing hardcoding.
- Documentation in SKILL.md and README.md clarified to emphasize dynamic whitelist workflow.
- Improved state/profile handling for firewall rules; whitelist.sh manages state—even on hash mismatches.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawd-zero-trust
Version: 1.1.9

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle 'clawd-zero-trust' is designed for security hardening and egress filtering. Its code and documentation are transparent and align with its stated purpose. Key indicators of benign intent include explicit mitigation of dynamic code execution (`eval` replaced with direct `"$@"` in `egress-filter.sh`), detailed documentation of known false positives for security scanners (`references/false-positives.md`), and the use of local logging for all actions. While the skill performs high-privilege operations (e.g., modifying UFW rules, OpenClaw configuration via `sudo`), these actions are directly in service of applying a zero-trust security policy, with transactional apply and rollback mechanisms. No evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, malicious execution, persistence, or prompt injection attempts against the agent was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and requests line up with its stated Zero Trust hardening purpose — it modifies OpenClaw config and host firewall rules and requires administrator action, which is coherent with the description.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Zero Trust hardening) match the actual code and instructions: scripts perform auditing, merge hardening.json into openclaw.json, manage PLP policies, and create DNS-based UFW egress allowlists. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or unexpected third-party services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs running local scripts that modify system state: UFW firewall rules (egress-filter.sh), openclaw.json (harden.sh / plp-config.sh), and writes state/log files under the skill workspace. It also performs network checks to external provider endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, Telegram) to verify connectivity after applying policy. This scope is expected for a hardening tool, but it requires admin privileges (sudo for ufw) and will change global agent config — operators should review scripts and run in dry-run first.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction + shipped scripts only (no downloads). That minimizes supply-chain risk. Scripts are included in the skill bundle and run locally; there are no remote installers or archive downloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. It does read and modify OpenClaw config and uses system tools (ufw, curl, dig, tailscale) and writes state under the skill directory. Modifying openclaw.json and firewall rules is proportional to a hardening tool, but these are high-privilege operations — ensure you trust the skill before granting sudo or letting it run with write access to OpenClaw configuration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced always-on). The skill writes its own .state files and logs under the skill workspace and can merge changes into the agent-wide openclaw.json. That level of persistence is expected for a hardening skill but does grant it the ability to change global agent configuration and firewall state when executed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: audit, harden, and enforce egress for an OpenClaw instance. Before installing or running it, do the following: 1) Review the scripts (egress-filter.sh, harden.sh, whitelist.sh, plp-config.sh) yourself — they modify openclaw.json and UFW and require sudo to apply policy. 2) Always run dry-run modes first (harden.sh and egress-filter.sh default to dry-run). 3) Be cautious with whitelist.sh: it appends entries to providers.txt and immediately runs the apply path with sudo, so only whitelist domains you trust. 4) Confirm you trust the listed external endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, Telegram, agentsandbox.co) because the script will verify connectivity to them and will whitelist/allow them for egress. 5) Test in a staging environment or take backups (openclaw.json backups are already part of harden.sh) before applying to production. If you need a deeper review (e.g., to verify network requests or UFW rule contents), provide the full untruncated egress-filter.sh file and the current providers.txt and I can point to any lines that would open specific ports/CIDRs.
